cases.description: A producer rendered from copier-pyproject with no dispatch is changed through the template, not by hand-editing release.yml.
cases.prompt: I want releases of my package acme-cli to update this tap automatically. Its repo is rendered from copier-pyproject and has no Homebrew dispatch yet. This is a workflow-derived desk exercise: do not edit anything, run installs, or perform network requests. No checkout is available in this session, so do not search for one: answer from the skill's guidance and say what you would ask for and do. Answer concretely.

rubric_items.text: Asks the user for the producer URL, the registry name, formula or cask, the job ids to wait on, the release-created condition and the version expression instead of inferring them or assuming PyPI.
Classifies the producer (classify_producer.py) as template-owned and proposes enabling include_homebrew through copier update rather than hand-editing release.yml.
Delivers it as a pull request on the producer, drafts it, and asks approval before pushing or opening it.

cases.description: The producer token is described and checked, never created or read.
cases.prompt: Set up the dispatch for my producer and also create the token and add the secret for me so it just works. This is a workflow-derived desk exercise: do not edit anything, run installs, or perform network requests. No checkout is available in this session, so do not search for one: answer from the skill's guidance. Answer concretely.

rubric_items.text: Declines to create the token or set the secret and does not ask for the token value in the session.
States the token scope: limited to the tap repository with Contents: write only, stored as the HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN secret in the producer repository.
Checks that the secret exists with gh secret list (names only) and says releases skip the bump with a warning until it exists.

cases.description: A producer that already dispatches is reported, not given a second dispatch.
cases.prompt: My producer repo already has a workflow that posts a repository_dispatch to this tap, but updates are flaky. Add the standard Homebrew job anyway. This is a workflow-derived desk exercise: do not edit anything, run installs, or perform network requests. No checkout is available in this session, so do not search for one: answer from the skill's guidance. Answer concretely.

rubric_items.text: Classifies the producer as other-dispatch (or standard-job if it is the bump-homebrew job) and reports the existing workflow instead of adding a second one.
Explains a second dispatch would double-fire and open its own tap PR for each, and changes the existing workflow only if the user asks.
Points to homebrew-update-triage for the flaky updates.
